elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause opens "On expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall ...", capturing every exit route, including the partial subscription terminations contemplated by 10.1.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "at Customer's request, provide transition assistance for up to six months after that expiry or termination". The request condition is general (not tied only to anticipated expiry) and the period is anchored to the actual expiry/termination date.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "within thirty days after that expiry or termination, return all Customer Data" — the 30-day clock runs from termination, not from a request.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "return all Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format".

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "after that return, delete Customer Data from its systems and certify the deletion in writing" — deletion is expressly sequenced after return.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same opening words: "On expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Up to six months of assistance exceeds the 90-day fallback floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return of all Customer Data within thirty days after expiry or termination.

reasons: All six preferred elements are met by a single inserted paragraph; the position is complete at the preferred level (and a fortiori at the fallback).

Minimality holds: the insertion is a concise new clause for a missing obligation, nothing in 10.1, 10.2 or 16.5 is deleted or paraphrased, and no extras (survival tail, at-own-expense, escrow, procedures, additional remedies) are bolted on.

Extending the trigger to "any Order Form" is not an extra requirement: 10.1 already contemplates termination of individual subscription Services, so the scoping keeps the assistance and return duties operative on partial exits rather than adding a new commercial term.

Intent is preserved: the refund and Deliverable mechanics in 10.2, the access wind-down in 10.1, and the confidentiality return/destroy regime in 16.5 (with its backup and legal-retention carve-outs) all survive without contradiction; the new clause supplies the Customer Data duties 16.5 expressly leaves to other sections.

Residual, pre-existing defect not created by this edit but worth a one-line note to the counterparty: 16.5 refers Customer Data out to "Sections 11 and 15" and there is no Section 11 in the Agreement. Consider asking that the cross-reference be repointed to the new transition clause so the retained sentence does not dangle.
